title: OneDrive and SharePoint: single hero link for file and folder sharing
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's supplied rollout notice. The documented sharing behaviour, administrative paths and PowerShell commands are supported, and the briefing explicitly preserves the documentation disagreements over OneDrive support and supported audience values.

claims.claim: Each OneDrive and SharePoint file or folder has one hero link.
claims.quote: In OneDrive and SharePoint, each item has one **hero link**.

claims.claim: Microsoft is introducing a replacement sharing dialog centred on the hero link.
claims.quote: Every file and folder will have a single primary sharing link, called the hero link, displayed in the sharing dialog.

claims.claim: Microsoft calls this the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience.
claims.quote: We're introducing the third-generation Microsoft 365 sharing experience to make collaboration simpler, smarter, and more secure by default.

claims.claim: The consistent sharing experience covers copied links, email sharing and the browser URL.
claims.quote: Users will see one consistent sharing experience whether they copy a link, share through email, or use the browser URL.

claims.claim: Users can change the hero link's audience without creating a new URL.
claims.quote: A hero link allows users to share a single link for an item, then change the audience and permissions for that link without needing to create a new URL.

claims.claim: Users can change the hero link's permissions without creating a new URL.
claims.quote: Changing the scope or permission doesn't create a new URL.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Add people remains a separate sharing method that grants direct access.
claims.quote: Users can share an item with specific people or security groups through **Add people**. This action grants direct access to the item.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The hero link starts at Only people added to the file by default.
claims.quote: By default, the hero link is set to Only people added to the file, meaning the link itself does not grant access to anyone.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Only people added to the file grants no additional access through the link itself.
claims.quote: At this scope, the link works for people who already have access, such as through a direct permission, a group, or the parent folder or site. It grants no additional access.

claims.claim: Users can give hero link recipients view permission.

claims.quote: A file inherits its folder's hero link settings until the file's own hero link is explicitly set or changed. After that, the file's hero link settings are independent.

claims.claim: Available hero link audience scopes depend on the organisation's sharing policies.
claims.quote: The audience *scope* determines who can use the hero link. Available scopes depend on the organization's sharing policies.

claims.claim: Anyone with the link permits access without signing in.
claims.quote: Anyone who receives the link can use it without signing in, including people outside the organization.

claims.claim: Anonymous link use cannot be audited to a named user.
claims.quote: Anyone can forward the link, and anonymous use can't be audited to a named user.

claims.claim: Selecting an audience scope does not itself make the item searchable or accessible through Copilot for everyone.
claims.quote: Selecting this scope doesn't grant organization-wide access or make the item available in search or Copilot for everyone in the organization.

claims.claim: A recipient must receive and redeem the link to establish link-based access and searchability.

claims.claim: Items shared through Add people can appear in search results for selected users and security group members, subject to permissions.
claims.quote: The item can appear in search results and is accessible through Copilot for selected users and security group members, subject to their permissions.

claims.claim: Items shared through Add people are accessible through Copilot for selected users and security group members, subject to permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Effective access is the highest permission granted by direct access, groups, parent folders or sites, the hero link or other sharing links.
claims.quote: A user's effective access is the highest permission granted by any source: direct access, a group, the parent folder or site, the hero link, or another sharing link.

claims.claim: Restricting the hero link does not remove access from other sources, which must each be changed to reduce effective access.
claims.quote: Reducing access requires changing each source that grants a higher permission.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite requires both SharePoint Online administrator and site collection administrator rights.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Online administrator and be a site collection administrator to run the cmdlet.

claims.where: controls[0].api; summary; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site URL> -DefaultMainLinkScope <OnlyPeopleAdded|Organization|Anyone> sets the site's default hero link audience.
claims.quote: The default audience for main links used in sharing. Applies to all items at the root of the document library. Only audience scope is set by this parameter.

claims.claim: No administrative UI for setting the site's default hero link audience is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link DefaultMainLinkScope admin center default audience tenant UI; "DefaultMainLinkScope" "admin center" "tenant". Read shareable-links, Set-SPOSite and change-default-sharing-link; only PowerShell documents the hero default.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-wide default hero link audience setting is currently documented on either administrative surface.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link DefaultMainLinkScope admin center default audience tenant UI; "DefaultMainLinkScope" "admin center" "tenant". Read MC1454378, shareable-links and Set-SPOTenant; the notice explicitly says there is no tenant-wide equivalent.

claims.claim: The Set-SPOTenant reference lists no main link parameter at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "DefaultMainLinkScope" "admin center" "tenant". Opened the complete Set-SPOTenant reference and searched its text for MainLink, main link and hero; no matches.

claims.claim: Organisation-level external sharing is configured in SharePoint admin center > Policies > Sharing.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand **Policies**, and then select **Sharing**.

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -SharingCapability <value> controls the organisation's sharing capability.
claims.quote:
### -SharingCapability

Determines what level of sharing is available for OneDrive and SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: The site's default sharing link type is under SharePoint admin center > Active sites > site > Sharing > Default sharing link type.
claims.quote:
In the left column, select a site.
3. Select **Sharing** on the command bar.
4. Under **Default sharing link type**, clear the **Same as organization-level setting** checkbox.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site URL> -DefaultSharingLinkType <value> sets the site's legacy default sharing link type.
claims.quote:
### -DefaultSharingLinkType

The default link type for the site collection. To be replaced by DefaultShareLinkScope.

claims.claim: The site-level default audience is the only documented administrative control specific to the hero link itself.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link DefaultMainLinkScope admin center default audience tenant UI. Read MC1454378, shareable-links, Set-SPOSite and Set-SPOTenant; no other hero-specific administrative setting found; default permission is not configurable.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: DefaultMainLinkScope sets only the starting audience and does not prevent users broadening access where policy permits.
claims.quote: DefaultMainLinkScope controls only the default audience and does not prevent users from broadening access when allowed by policy.

claims.claim: MC1454378 lists OnlyPeopleAdded as the default and Organization as the other supported DefaultMainLinkScope value.
claims.quote: Supported values are:- OnlyPeopleAdded (default)- Organization

claims.claim: The Set-SPOSite reference additionally permits Anyone and documents fallback when Anyone links are disabled for the site.
claims.quote:
The valid values are:

- OnlyPeopleAdded
- Organization
- Anyone

`Anyone` is only available if anonymous links are allowed at the tenant level. If `Anyone` is selected but the site has Anyone links disabled, the effective default falls back to the next most restrictive value.

claims.claim: DefaultMainLinkScope applies to all items at the root of the document library.
claims.quote: Applies to all items at the root of the document library.

claims.claim: In contrast to the cmdlet's valid-parameter list, MC1454378 explicitly describes configuring the default at OneDrive level.
claims.quote: Administrators can configure the default audience for the hero link at the SharePoint site collection or OneDrive level by using the DefaultMainLinkScope parameter in SharePoint PowerShell.

claims.claim: A site's external sharing setting must be the same as or more restrictive than the organisation's.
claims.quote: Each site has its own sharing setting that you can set independently, though it must be at the same or more restrictive setting as the organization.

claims.claim: The new sharing experience arrives on by default rather than requiring administrator opt-in.
claims.quote:
Who is affected: All users who share or manage files and folders in Microsoft 365.

No action is required before rollout.

claims.claim: A sender can expand access on the same hero link when recipients cannot open a previously shared file.
claims.quote: If recipients cannot open a previously shared file, the sender can expand access on the same hero link without redistributing a new URL.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a complete mapping of individual sharing policy settings to available hero link scopes.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint hero link DefaultMainLinkScope admin center default audience tenant UI. Read shareable-links, turn-external-sharing-on-or-off and Set-SPOSite: policy dependency and the Anyone prerequisite are stated, but no complete hero-scope mapping was found.

claims.claim: DefaultMainLinkScope's Anyone value requires anonymous links to be allowed at tenant level.
claims.quote: `Anyone` is only available if anonymous links are allowed at the tenant level.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends communicating the updated sharing experience to regular cross-team and cross-organisation collaborators.
claims.quote: Communicate the updated sharing experience to users who regularly collaborate across teams and organizations.

claims.quote: Evaluate site-level default sharing settings where different sharing behaviors are required.
